# Requirements Document: Choosing seats

## Introduction

A seller asks for a seat map, which marks each seat of a flight available or
occupied, and chooses seats for passengers.  Each seat chosen becomes its own
order item at the seat's price, holding one seat service for the passenger on
that segment, as in the seat worked example.  The guide states no rule that a
seat goes to one passenger only, or that a passenger holds one seat per
segment; the model checks each choice against the seat map and nothing else.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Seats.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Seats.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-605

**User Story:** As a passenger, I want the seat I chose to be mine alone, so that I do not find someone else in it.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller chooses seats for passengers THE SYSTEM SHALL add one order item for each seat the seat map marks available, and refuse the request if any seat chosen is not. (Lean: `chooseSeats`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF a seat choice names a seat that the seat map of its segment does not mark available THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the request.
   - ONE-605.1, proven: proven theorem `choose_seats_refuses_unavailable`; example `occupiedSeatRefused`
2. WHEN a seat request is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the existing order items and add one order item for each seat chosen, at the seat's price, holding one seat service for that passenger on that segment.
   - ONE-605.2, proven: proven theorem `choose_seats_items`; example `sameSeatTwice`; example `secondSeatSamePassenger`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL never let two passengers hold the same seat on the same segment.
   - ONE-605.3, open: open theorem `choose_seats_one_passenger_per_seat`; counterexample `sameSeatTwice`
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL let a passenger hold at most one live seat on each segment.
   - ONE-605.4, open: open theorem `choose_seats_one_seat_per_passenger`; counterexample `secondSeatSamePassenger`

#### Open question on ONE-605.3

> When no seat is held by two passengers on a segment, and the seat maps mark
> no held seat available, an accepted seat request keeps it so.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide checks a seat choice against the
> seat map and states no rule that a seat goes to one passenger.  One request
> that chooses 12B on the same flight for two passengers passes, since the seat
> map marks 12B available for each choice.  The example `sameSeatTwice`
> shows it.  Is a seat checked against the other choices of the same request,
> against every order on the flight, or only against the seat map?  And is the
> unit the passenger segment or the leg the aircraft flies?

#### Open question on ONE-605.4

> When each passenger holds at most one seat on each segment, and the seat
> maps mark no held seat available, an accepted seat request keeps it so.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide does not say whether choosing a
> seat replaces a seat the passenger already holds.  A passenger who holds 12B
> and chooses 14A in a second request holds both, each in its own active order
> item.  The example `secondSeatSamePassenger` shows it.  May a passenger
> hold an extra seat, for comfort or for a large instrument, and does choosing a
> new seat cancel the old one, with what refund?
